intent: Group related rows of a context menu under one optional ContextMenuLabel.
typical_uses: A captioned block of related actions inside a menu popup

dont_use_when.situation: A set of options of which exactly one is selected
A visual break between items with no caption

invariants.text: The group renders `role="group"` and takes its accessible name from the ContextMenuLabel inside it, through `aria-labelledby`, unless the caller passes its own `aria-labelledby`; a group with neither has no name.
context-menu.module.css gives the group no class; it adds no spacing or divider around its items.

children.states: children is the group's label and rows
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the group's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (an empty object for a group). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A captioned group of edit actions
Two groups divided by a separator

bad.title: A group used to hold a single-choice setting
bad.why: ContextMenuRadioItem reads its selection from the nearest ContextMenuRadioGroup and the primitive throws without one; a plain group holds no value. Use ContextMenuRadioGroup instead.

children.description: TS: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. children is the group's label and rows. `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, MenuGroupState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: MenuGroupState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the group's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (an empty object for a group). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.
